2027-01-31.title: Aneede Sunday · Commemoration of the Departed Faithful
readings: Jacob is gathered to his people
New heavens and a new earth
We will be with the Lord for ever
The dead will hear the voice of the Son of God
2027-01-31.alt: Aneede Sunday: the Church remembers all the faithful departed. The Great Fast begins next Sunday.
2027-01-31.verse: Very truly, I tell you, anyone who hears my word and believes him who sent me has eternal life, and does not come under judgment, but has passed from death to life.
theo: Last Sunday we remembered the departed priests; today, Aneede Sunday, we remember all the faithful departed: our parents and grandparents, brothers and sisters, children and friends. The Church does not forget them. Before we enter the Great Fast, we gather them in prayer, because Lent leads to Easter, the victory of Christ over death.

Jesus says: “The hour is coming, and is now here, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live… all who are in their graves will hear his voice and will come out.” St Paul writes to the Thessalonians so “that you may not grieve as others do who have no hope.” Christian grief is real, but it is grief with hope: “so we will be with the Lord forever.”

The reading from 2 Maccabees shows that God's people prayed for the dead even before Christ. Judas Maccabeus took up a collection for a sin offering for the fallen, “for if he were not expecting that those who had fallen would rise again, it would have been superfluous and foolish to pray for the dead”. From the beginning the Church has prayed for the departed and offered the Holy Qurbono for them, that they may be purified and enter the joy of God.

The evening Gospel reminds us how we will be judged: “I was hungry and you gave me food… just as you did it to one of the least of these who are members of my family, you did it to me.” The best way to honour our dead is to pray for them and to live in such a way that, when our turn comes, we too may hear: “Come, you that are blessed by my Father.”
conn: Jacob “breathed his last, and was gathered to his people” (Genesis 49:33): death is a gathering, not an ending.
2 Maccabees 12:45 is the Old Testament root of the Church's prayer for the departed (CCC 1032).
“You have held back my life from the pit of destruction, for you have cast all my sins behind your back” (Isaiah 38:17): God's mercy reaches beyond death.
New heavens and a new earth.
2 Peter 3:13 and Revelation 21:1: our hope is not only for souls but for a renewed creation and the resurrection of the body.
altar: In every Holy Qurbono, in the Thubden, the Church remembers the faithful departed by name. Today we offer the Qurbono for all our dead: the Body and Blood of the risen Lord are the pledge of their resurrection and ours.
outline: Invite the people to name silently those they have lost.
1 Thessalonians 4: not as those who have no hope.
Point 2 · Why we pray for the dead
2 Maccabees 12; the Church's tradition; the Qurbono for the departed.
Matthew 25: the hungry, the stranger, the sick, the prisoner.
Lent is the journey to the Resurrection.
“We will be with the Lord forever.”
live: Write the names of your departed family members and pray for them each day this week; offer a Qurbono for them.
Visit the graves of your family, clean them, and pray there.
Feed, visit or clothe someone this week in memory of a departed loved one.
fathers: His mother Monica asked as she was dying: “Lay this body anywhere; only this I ask of you, that you remember me at the altar of the Lord, wherever you may be” (Confessions IX, 11).
“Let us help and commemorate them… Why would you doubt that our offerings for the dead bring them some consolation?” (Homilies on 1 Corinthians 41).
magis: Those who die in God's grace but still imperfectly purified undergo purification; the Church commends prayer, the Eucharistic sacrifice, almsgiving and works of penance for them.
The Christian funeral and the communion of saints with the departed.
The union of the pilgrim Church with those who have died in Christ is not broken, but strengthened by the sharing of spiritual goods.
saints: 31 Jan: St John Bosco. 2 Feb (Tuesday): Mayaltho, the Entrance of our Lord into the Temple. 3 Feb: Mar Simon and Morth Hanna. 4 Feb: St John de Britto.
2027-01-31.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you are the resurrection and the life. Remember all our departed brothers and sisters, our parents, relatives, friends and benefactors, and those whom no one remembers. Forgive their sins, give them eternal rest, and let perpetual light shine upon them. Amen.

quick: Aneede Sunday: we remember all the faithful departed.
Christian grief has hope: we will be with the Lord for ever.
We will be judged on love: what we did for the least.
2027-01-31.action: Offer a Qurbono and pray daily this week for your departed family members.
2027-01-31.question: How am I preparing for my own meeting with the Lord?
2027-01-31.special: Aneede Sunday, commemoration of the faithful departed. Announce the beginning of the Great Fast with Kothine Sunday (7 February) and the Shubkono on Monday 8 February. Catholicos Day, with its collection, is kept on Kothine Sunday, 7 February.
illus: In Kerala families the name of a departed parent is written in the parish register for the annual Qurbono, and the family gathers every year on that day. Love does not stop at the grave; it becomes prayer.

family.explain: When people we love die, we are sad. But Jesus rose from the dead, and he will raise them too. We pray for them so that they may be happy with God.
family.intention: We pray for our grandparents and all our family members who have died.
family.ask: Ask: “Who in our family has gone to God? Let us tell one good memory of them.”

kidsaint: The mother of St Augustine, who prayed for her son for many years until he came back to God. Before she died she asked him only to remember her at the altar. Lesson: pray for those you love, living and dead.
term: Aneede is Syriac for “the departed”. On the Sunday before the Great Fast the Malankara Church remembers all the faithful departed, after remembering the departed priests on Kohne Sunday.
termMore: Why do we pray for the dead?
Because love does not end with death, and because the dead who still need purification can be helped by the prayers and offerings of the living (2 Maccabees 12:45; CCC 1032).

pm.open: Lord Jesus, resurrection and life, today we remember all the faithful departed. Grant them rest and light, and keep us in hope. Amen.
share: Anyone who hears my word… has eternal life (John 5:24). Do I live with eternal life in view?
Just as you did it to one of the least of these… you did it to me (Matthew 25:40). Whom is Christ asking me to serve?
Judas Maccabeus made atonement for the dead (2 Maccabees 12:45). Do I pray faithfully for my departed relatives?
interc: For all our departed parents, grandparents, relatives and friends.
For those who died this year, and for their families.
For the souls who have no one to pray for them.
For the dying, that they may meet Christ in peace.
For our group, that we may prepare well for the Great Fast.
pm.close: Father, in your Son you have given us hope of resurrection. Grant rest to the departed and keep us faithful until we meet them again. Through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, last Sunday we remembered our departed priests. Today, Aneede Sunday, we remember all our faithful departed. Let us take a moment of silence and bring to mind those we have lost: a father, a mother, a husband, a wife, a child, a friend.

St Paul writes: we do not want you to grieve “as others do who have no hope”. He does not say “do not grieve”. Jesus himself wept at the tomb of his friend. But our grief has hope, because Christ is risen. Jesus says: “All who are in their graves will hear his voice and will come out.” One day our dead will hear that voice.

Why do we pray for the dead? Our reading from Maccabees says: if Judas had not believed in the resurrection, it would have been foolish to pray for the fallen. The Church has always prayed and offered the Holy Qurbono for the departed, that they may be purified and enter fully into God's joy. St Monica asked her son Augustine only one thing before she died: “Remember me at the altar of the Lord.”

And the evening Gospel reminds us how we ourselves will be judged: “I was hungry and you gave me food… as you did it to one of the least of these, you did it to me.” Next Sunday the Great Fast begins. Let us enter it remembering that life is short, that love is what remains, and that we too are walking towards the Lord. Eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord. Amen.
kids: Children, do you have a grandpa or grandma who has gone to God? Today we remember all the people we love who have died.
We feel sad, but we also have hope, because Jesus rose from the dead and he will bring them to new life.
Tonight, pray for them by name. Let's say: “Jesus, keep them happy with you in heaven!”

intro: On Aneede Sunday we remember all our departed: parents, grandparents, friends. We do not come as people without hope. We come to pray for them and to learn from them how to live.

points.h: In Christ, death is a passage to life
sub: Jacob ended his blessing, breathed his last and was “gathered to his people”.
Jesus promises: whoever hears his word and believes has already passed from death to life.
Our departed are not lost; they are on the way home, and we pray that they reach it.
q: When Jacob ended his charge to his sons, he drew up his feet into the bed, breathed his last, and was gathered to his people.
Very truly, I tell you, anyone who hears my word and believes him who sent me has eternal life, and does not come under judgment, but has passed from death to life.
points.apply: Name your departed loved ones in prayer each day this week.

sub: Hezekiah, facing death, turned to God and found mercy.
St Paul does not forbid grief; he forbids grief without hope.
The Church prays for the dead, that they may be purified and see God; this is an act of love (CCC 1032).
q: Surely it was for my welfare that I had great bitterness; but you have held back my life from the pit of destruction, for you have cast all my sins behind your back.

We do not want you to be uninformed … about those who have died, so that you may not grieve as others do who have no hope. For since we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so, through Jesus, God will bring with him those who have died.
points.apply: Have a Holy Qurbono offered for your departed, and visit the cemetery with your family.

points.h: We will be judged by love
sub: At the last judgment the King asks about the hungry, the stranger, the sick and the prisoner.
Proverbs says kindness to the poor is a loan to the Lord.
The best way to honour our dead is to live the works of mercy they taught us.
q: Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the LORD, and will be repaid in full.
Truly I tell you, just as you did it to one of the least of these who are members of my family, you did it to me.
points.apply: Do one work of mercy this week in memory of a departed loved one.

concl: The dead hear the voice of the Son of God; those who have done good will rise to life.
Let us pray for our departed with faith and live with charity, so that one day we may meet them in the Father's house.
2027-01-31.resolve: Pray “Eternal rest grant to them, O Lord” for the departed after each meal this week.
